thread:
incident-bot: Paging on-call — high GPU utilization in dedicated pool 'solace-vpc-prod'. 9/10 GPUs at 96%. Single tenant 'solace' accounts for >85% of active allocations. Alert INC-2026-345. https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-345

Liam S.: On it. Investigating. @Tom R. can you check the autoscaler and tenant burst config?

Tom R.: Looking. I see a large batch/backfill from tenant_id=solace. Autoscaler shows max_nodes=10 reached and we have "burst_limit_reached" in the logs.

Sara K.: Checked tenant settings — burst: disabled for solace-vpc-prod. That explains no overflow to shared.

Priya M.: (Priya from CS) I just heard from Solace: they kicked off a scheduled backfill this morning and it's still running. Their production latency is degrading and they asked for temporary extra capacity.

Maya N.: Options: 1) enable tenant burst (allow controlled overflow to shared capacity), 2) approve emergency add of reserved nodes (slow, infra >30m), 3) request customer pause/backoff. Need quick decision.

Liam S.: My preference: enable burst with a tight cap (2-3 shared nodes) so other tenants not impacted. Also enable short-term per-tenant throttle if we see noisy endpoints.

Tom R.: We can flip burst via admin API. Example:

```
curl -u admin:*** -X POST \"https://admin.redwood.internal/tenants/solace/burst\" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"enable": true, "allowed_shared_nodes": 3}'
```

If we do that, autoscaler should allow up to 3 shared nodes for solace and queued tasks can drain.

Priya M. (solace-sre): Solace confirms they can pause the backfill if notified. They prefer we enable capacity first so they can continue critical portions.

Liam S.: I'm going to enable burst with allowed_shared_nodes=3 now. If utilization stays >90% for 10m after change, we trigger eviction/throttle plan.

Tom R.: Executing admin call now. Response: 200 OK, {"status":"success","enabled":true,"allowed_shared_nodes":3}.

incident-bot: Configuration change logged (INC-2026-345): burst enabled for tenant solace by Liam S..

Maya N.: Also recommend enabling tenant-level prefix KV cache to lower per-token compute for their common prompts. Small config change, low risk.

Liam S.: Enabling cache:
```
curl -u admin:*** -X POST \"https://admin.redwood.internal/tenants/solace/cache\" -d '{"prefix_kv":true, "ttl_secs":3600}'
```
Response: 200 OK.

Tom R.: Metrics update: queued tasks dropped 1200 -> ~180 within 6 minutes. GPU utilization dropped from 96% -> 78% across pool, shared nodes now 3 and active. No other tenants reporting errors.

Priya M. (solace-sre): We've paused the non-critical part of the backfill for 15 minutes to be safe. We'll resume in coordination if needed. Thanks.

Sara K.: Recording action items for RCA: 1) review default burst policy for enterprise VPCs (Ow: Tom), 2) add early CS notification at 80% sustained utilization (Ow: Priya), 3) validate autoscale upper bounds vs expected tenant workloads (Ow: Sara).

Maya N.: For billing/credits: CS, please capture request and time window so finance can evaluate emergency capacity credit.

Liam S.: Monitoring window: I'll watch for 30m and prepare escalation to infra if usage trends back up. Current pool GPU utilization 62%, queued 0. Leaving enhanced monitors on. Tagging #oncall #mitigation.

Liam S.: Handoff in 1h to @OncallTomorrow — system stable, burst enabled, shared nodes=3, cache enabled. If we see >85% sustained for 10m, page immediately.

OncallTomorrow: Acknowledge. I'll take over monitoring and the open action items.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 mitigation in place: burst enabled, cache enabled, customer contacted and partial job paused. Monitoring continues.

Sara K.: Closing notes: short-term mitigation successful. Next steps: policy changes + automated CS alerts + post-incident review scheduled tomorrow 10:00am PT.

Liam S.: Thanks team — handing off.
